newsitem.title: TAIWAN: U.S. Fed OKs Taiwan Sinopac takeover of U.S. bank.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Fed OKs Taiwan Sinopac takeover of U.S. bank.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Reserve has given approval to Taiwan's Bank Sinopac to set up a U.S. holding company to buy California-based Far East National Bank, Sinopac said on Thursday.
Sinopac gave no details of the Fed action.

Taiwan's finance ministry on June 2 approved the US$80 million takeover despite what it called "complications" arising from Far East's operations in communist China, the longtime arch rival of Taiwan's Chinese Nationalist government.
The ministry said the approval should be viewed as an individual case and not a precedent for other Taiwan banks eyeing mainland investments.
Deeply wary of becoming overdependent on the economy of its longtime rival, Taiwan explicitly bans investment by local interests in mainland banks and other financial institutions.

Finance minister Paul Chiu made clear Taipei did not regard Far East National's Beijing office as a financial institution since it operates only as a liaison office and does not take deposits or make loans.

Beijing has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949, but a late 1980s thaw in their once-icy relations has allowed economic ties to flourish, with Taiwan firms investing some US$30 billion in the mainland.
